subject: physics
question_text: A mass of 2 kg is attached to a spring of force constant 200 Nm⁻¹. Find its time period.

verification.note: Printed as the applied half of an 8-mark Section-C question in TS March 2019 (Q20), Inter I-Year Physics Paper-I. The 4-mark standalone length is our authoring choice, not the board's — the board never printed it as a 4-mark Section-B question. Arithmetic hand-checked: m/k = 2/200 = 0.01, and kg/(N m⁻¹) = s², so the ratio is 0.01 s²; √0.01 = 0.1 s; T = 2π × 0.1 = 0.2π ≈ 0.628 s. The derivation of T = 2π√(m/k) itself is the companion card ts_ipe_p1_osc_spring_frequency; this card applies the result. The three-way split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The formula
lines: For a mass m on a spring of force constant
Here m = 2 kg and k = 200 N m⁻¹.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The formula with m and k named, before any arithmetic.
steps.why: Only the mass and the force constant set the period of a loaded spring. The amplitude and the value of g do not appear in the formula, which is why the question supplies no other number.
common_mistakes: Writing T = 2π√(k/m), which inverts the ratio and gives 62.8 s, a hundred times too large.
Bringing g into the formula. The period of a loaded spring does not contain g.

recall.must_convey: That T = 2 pi root m by k, with m = 2 kg and k = 200 newton per metre.
accept: T is two pi root m by k
mass by force constant inside the root
two kg and two hundred newton per metre
reject: zero point six two eight second

steps.memory_tip: Heavier mass, slower swing: m sits on TOP inside the root of T = 2π√(m/k).

steps.label: The ratio and its root
lines: Take the ratio first and check its unit:

lines.text: kg / (N m⁻¹) = s², so √(m/k) is in s

steps.margin_note: Second mark. The ratio and its square root. The unit check earns it.
steps.why: The ratio m/k has the unit s², so its square root is a time and the answer comes out in seconds with no further conversion. Doing the division and the root before touching 2π leaves one multiplication for the last step.
common_mistakes: Writing √0.01 = 0.001. The square root of 0.01 is 0.1.
Squaring the ratio instead of taking its square root.

recall.must_convey: That m by k is 0.01 s², and its square root is 0.1 s.
accept: two by two hundred is zero point zero one
root of point zero one is point one
the ratio has unit second squared
reject: T is two pi root m by k

steps.memory_tip: 2/200 = 0.01 and √0.01 = 0.1 s. Two decimal places become one.

steps.label: The time period
lines: That is about 1.6 oscillations a second.
steps.margin_note: Third and fourth marks. Evaluate 0.2π and write the unit s beside it.
steps.why: 2π ≈ 6.28, so 2π × 0.1 ≈ 0.628 s. The question asks for the time period, so the answer has to be a number of seconds; the symbolic 0.2π on its own is not the value that was asked for.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as 0.2π when the question asks for a value.
Giving the frequency, about 1.6 Hz, in place of the time period.

accept: zero point six two eight second
two pi into zero point one
reject: root of point zero one is point one

steps.memory_tip: 2π ≈ 6.28, so 2π × 0.1 ≈ 0.628 s. The decimal point moves one place.

insider_note: Two of the four marks are the final value, and the second of them is earned only when 0.2π is evaluated to 0.628 s with its unit.
